name: Banasura Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Hill forest of southwestern india (western ghats in coorg region)
description: This is the only montane laughingthrush in its range and hence unmistakable. It is dull brown above, with gray breast and head and a pale rufous belly.

name: Tibetan Serin
rangeDescription: Coniferous forest of northern india to nepal, eastern tibet, and southwestern china
description: Bright yellow finch of foothill and montane coniferous and mixed forests. Male is greenish-yellow above and bright yellow below.

name: Swierstra's Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western angola (cuanza sul to huila)
description: Rare and unusual francolin that is endemic to Angola. Note the red bill and legs, mostly white face, black breast band, and black-striped white underparts.

name: Giant Wren
rangeDescription: Humid pacific lowlands of southern mexico (chiapas)
description: Very large wren restricted to coastal plain of Chiapas and adjacent Guatemala. Favors open and semiopen areas with hedges, scattered large trees, stone walls, and thickets; often in and around villages and in gardens of small farms.

name: Ivory Gull
rangeDescription: Arctic circumpolar (mainly associated with ice pack)
description: A spectacular and highly sought-after Arctic gull. Unmistakable in all plumages.

name: Iraq Babbler
rangeDescription: Southern türkiye, syria, iraq, and southwestern iran (reedbeds of tigris-euphrates valley)
description: Small babbler with a long tail and short wings, typical of other babblers. Warm buff overall with a pale throat and a lightly streaked back and crown.

name: Little Bunting
rangeDescription: Taiga of northern eurasia; winters to india, southeastern asia, and philippines
description: Small bunting with an attractive contrasting head pattern: black crown with red-brown central stripe and pale eyering. Rufous cheeks bordered by narrow black lines framing the eyes.

name: White-cheeked Starling
rangeDescription: Northeastern asia; winters in southern china and philippines
description: This rather grimy-looking species is a familiar presence in many open habitats. Dark gray-brown overall with white cheeks of varying size, usually streaked with dark gray; white sometimes covers most of the head.

name: Indian Courser
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed pakistan to india and sri lanka
description: Elegant and stately large plover-like bird. Note typically erect posture, strong black-and-white brow pattern, orange-suffused crown and chest, and slightly downcurved dark bill.

name: Javan Bulbul
rangeDescription: Montane forest of java
description: Sombrely-colored bulbul with a long slender bill, olive back and wings, well-streaked underparts, and a weak crest that is not always visible. Restricted to Javan highlands, where it can be found in pristine forests, as well as degraded forest and forest edge.

name: Serra do Mar Tyrant-Manakin
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southern minas gerais, rio de janeiro, and eastern são paulo)
description: Rather nondescript manakin that may resemble a flycatcher. Mostly olive green, but notable features include a yellow crown and paler chin.

name: Black-throated Saltator
rangeDescription: Campos of northeastern bolivia (beni eastward to santa cruz) to northeastern paraguay and interior northeastern and central brazil
description: Charismatic noisy inhabitant of savanna, Brazilian caatinga, and shrubby areas where it is easy to see, perching conspicuously on bushes and fence wires. Often accompanies mixed-species flocks.

name: Maned Owl
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed in humid forest of liberia to eastern democratic republic of the congo
description: Distinctive and unusual rainforest owl. Mostly rufous-brown, with long, shaggy ear tufts and plumes at the back of the head.

name: Sumatran Treepie
rangeDescription: Mountains of sumatra
description: A dapper and long-tailed inhabitant of Java’s foothill and montane forests. Warm brown overall, with a silvery nape, dark face, and jet-black wings marked with a small white patch.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Blue-tailed Bee-eater
rangeDescription: India to southern china, southeastern asia, new guinea, and indonesia
description: Elegant, slender bird of open country, frequently seen in flight or perched on exposed snags or telephone wires. Adult green overall, with blue tail, thin black mask, and rufous throat; bright rufous underwings visible in flight.

name: Jackson's Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western and central kenya
description: Large, chunky brown francolin with a red bill, red legs, and bare red skin around the eye. Found in montane forest, forest edge, moorland, and grassland.

name: Manchurian Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Northern manchuria; winters to southern china and thailand
description: Small, shy, and poorly understood, this reed warbler breeds in the remote marshlands of northeastern China and Russia and winters in drier, grassier habitats in Southeast Asia. Warm brown overall with a clean-cut whitish brow and throat; brow extends well behind the eye, unlike in Blunt-winged Warbler.

name: Tsavo Sunbird
rangeDescription: Southern somalia, eastern kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: Male is iridescent green above and dark below, with a narrow purple band across the breast. Female is nondescript, with a pale eyebrow and faint streaking across the pale underparts.

name: White-lined Antbird
rangeDescription: Far southwestern amazonian brazil to southeastern peru and northwestern bolivia
description: Large antbird of bamboo stands in river edge forest. Males are dark gray with bright white wing bars and a darker blackish crest that is raised when agitated; females appear two-toned: orange above, with creamy white face and underparts.

name: Purple-bearded Bee-eater
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sulawesi
description: An unmistakable large bee-eater with elongated central tail feathers, a green back and uppertail, and a diagnostic deep purple face and throat. Purple throat is more extensive in males.
